author: DTrim99
body:
Great questions — your intuition is right on both counts. References for the full mechanics:

- **RCW 82.08.0206(3)** — the controlling statute: [(3)(a)](https://app.leg.wa.gov/RCW/default.aspx?cite=82.08.0206) flat credit amounts by child count, **(3)(b)** the phase-out, **(3)(c)** the $50 minimum.
- **HB 1888 (2021)** — directs DOR to set the phase-out *rate* so the credit reaches the $50 minimum exactly at the maximum qualifying income. [Bill summary](https://app.leg.wa.gov/billsummary?BillNumber=1888&Year=2021).

**Does the credit start at the maximum regardless of earnings?** Yes — the WFTC has **no phase-in**. Unlike the federal EITC, the federal phase-in/phase-out rates (your .15/.18) don't size it. Per (3)(a) it's a flat maximum by qualifying-child count ($1,330 for 3+ children in TY2025), and the only adjustment is the phase-out near the top. So you start at $1,330 and subtract only once income enters the phase-out band.

**Your $2,000-earnings, 3-child example:** the full **$1,330**, provided the household otherwise qualifies for the federal EITC under the frozen June 9, 2022 rules (qualifying children, valid SSN/ITIN, investment income under the limit, earned income > $0). Worked numbers for MFJ, 3 children, 2025:

- Maximum qualifying income (frozen 2022 federal EITC completed-phaseout AGI) ≈ **$59,190**
- Phase-out band = **$5,000** → phase-out *starts* at ≈ **$54,190**
- Phase-out rate = ($1,330 − $50) / $5,000 = **25.6%** per dollar above the start
- Income below ~$54,190 → full **$1,330**; declining to the **$50** floor at $59,190; above that, no credit.

At $2,000 you're ~$52,000 below the phase-out start, so the full $1,330 applies.

**On income vs. earnings:** you're right — per (3)(b) the reduction is measured against the *federal phase-out income*, i.e. the **greater of earned income or AGI**, not earnings alone. And in checking this, your question surfaced a genuine bug in PolicyEngine: we currently compute the WFTC phase-out reduction on **earned income only**, while the eligibility ceiling correctly uses `max(earned income, AGI)`. For typical filers (earnings ≈ AGI) the results match, but a household with low earnings and substantial unearned income in the phase-out band — e.g. MFJ, 3 kids, $40k wages + $16k unemployment (AGI $56k) — currently gets the full $1,330 when the statute would taper it to ~$867. We're opening an issue in `policyengine-us` to fix it. Thanks for the catch.
